authorization_audit.theorem_status_not_user_authority: User approval may freeze a protocol but cannot turn an unproved mathematical premise into a theorem.
authorization_audit.user_goal: A fully provable deterministic P=NP algorithm; heuristics and finite tests are insufficient.
authorization_audit.user_bidirectional_requirement: JANUS should also support exact bidirectional traversal/direction switching as a stronger engineering/proof-carrying property, but this is not substituted for the core P=NP proof.

immutable_kernel_laws.law: P_VS_NP remains OPEN until a complete universal correctness and worst-case polynomial-time proof is independently checkable.
The theorem-mode algorithm, rewrite grammar, lane order, tie-breaking order, acceptance/rejection gates, verifier version and resource exponents are frozen before the input is seen.
Heuristics, ML, neural scores, randomized search, M2R forecasts, voting, confidence or empirical scaling may propose research candidates but may never commit a theorem-mode state transition.

The executable theorem-mode algorithm may not call a general SAT oracle, arbitrary semantic-equivalence oracle, free semantic canonizer, or any black box whose complexity already contains the target problem.

A transition may commit only after exact local replay verifies its guard, decision-preserving transformation, certificate, fixed-budget compliance and strict well-founded progress; failed candidates leave the frozen state unchanged.
When multiple exact admissible transitions exist, theorem mode selects by one frozen canonical order, never by semantic quality optimization.
All state, work and certificate bounds are measured against original input length N using fixed exponents; no step may rebase its budget on the current or expanded state.

The ledger counts successful and failed deterministic discovery work, clauses, factor/DAG nodes and edges, contexts/boundary states, auxiliary semantic variables, extension history, normalization microsteps, coefficient/integer bit lengths, certificate/proof bytes, verifier work, indexes and recovery payload.
Finite probes may refute frozen finite claims, but absence of a counterexample cannot establish universal asymptotic closure or P=NP.
The universal proof obligation concerns states reachable under the one frozen algorithm and its actual scheduled transitions.
Replacement, quotient and compilation steps require exact contextual semantics: interface equivalence, exact existential elimination, or proved conservative extension with projection.
Compact representations are admissible only when required terminal truth queries and scheduled transformations are polynomially executable and verifiable under the global envelope.
Existence of a useful exact representation or certificate is insufficient; the frozen algorithm must discover or recognize it in polynomial total work.
Strict macro progress does not excuse superpolynomial or cyclic internal normalization; a polynomial microstep bound is required.
Semantic Boolean variables, representation node IDs and definitional extension IDs are distinct typed resources; fresh extension IDs are never silently reused.
A family-specific polynomial lane may run only after exact polynomial structural recognition or a proved reduction.
An exploding generic representation refutes that representation path, not SAT tractability; exact already-frozen structural lanes may be tried with charged recognition cost.
If the frozen theorem machine reaches a grammar hole or lacks a certified move, the run returns OPEN; repairs require a new frozen algorithm version and fresh run.
M2R may forecast failures and TOPA may attack claims, but only exact replay/checkable derivation may promote theorem obligations.
Backward/future-first machinery transports frozen mathematical obligations or replay data, not physical future-to-past information.
Backward obligation transport may use only typed local polynomially verified pullback rules; generic weakest-precondition or inverse solving is forbidden unless separately proved polynomial.

Exact reversible transport may be required as a stronger JANUS property, but the core P=NP proof must stand on totality, exactness and global polynomial complexity without relying on free history storage.
If reversibility retains recovery data, cumulative recovery bytes and reverse work are charged to the original-N global envelope.
Positive theorem artifacts require independent deterministic verification; semantic, parameter, certificate and resource-binding tampering must be rejected.
The P=NP decision theorem is proved on exact SAT decision; witness recovery is a separate polynomial layer and must not become an accidental stronger hidden premise.
Frozen predictions, gates, thresholds, representation families and resource bounds are not moved after seeing results; failures remain preserved.
Frozen runs and historical artifacts are not rewritten; corrections and supersessions are new append-only events or versions.
A theorem proved for one family, cap, rung or representation language remains scoped there until a separate universal bridge is proved.

retro_audit_findings.remaining_blocker_is_mathematical_not_au: Universal reachable-state useful-action/GPEI preservation and its global polynomial proof remain OPEN.

current_central_theorem_target.name: UNIVERSAL_CERTIFIED_USEFUL_ACTION_GPEI
current_central_theorem_target.statement: For every arbitrary-CNF input phi and every nonterminal state S reachable under the one frozen deterministic JANUS algorithm, at least one canonically selectable exact certified action exists that preserves the original-N polynomial envelope and strict progress; total discovery, execution, normalization, certificate and verifier work and the number of macrosteps are bounded by fixed polynomials in |phi|.
